Describe the structure of BNF codes

Source: R/bnf.R
bnf_level.Rd

BNF codes are hierarchical: the first 2 characters give the chapter, 4 the section, 6 the paragraph, 7 the subparagraph, 9 the chemical substance, 11 the product and 15 the presentation. bnf_level() reports which level a code is, bnf_parent() truncates to a higher level, and bnf_class() returns a readable label for chapter 5 sections and paragraphs (antibacterial classes).

Usage

bnf_level(code)

bnf_parent(
  code,
  level = c("chemical", "section", "paragraph", "chapter", "subparagraph", "product")
)

bnf_class(code, at = c("paragraph", "section"))

Arguments

code

Character vector of BNF codes (any level).

level

For bnf_parent(): one of "chapter", "section", "paragraph", "subparagraph", "chemical", "product".

at

For bnf_class(): "paragraph" (default, e.g. 050101 Penicillins) or "section" (e.g. 0501 Antibacterial drugs).

Value

bnf_level() and bnf_class() return character vectors (NA where the code is not recognised); bnf_parent() returns the truncated codes (NA where the code is shorter than the requested level).

Examples

bnf_level(c("0501", "0501013B0", "0501013B0AAAAAA"))
#> [1] "section"      "chemical"     "presentation"
bnf_parent("0501013K0", "paragraph")
#> [1] "050101"
bnf_class(c("0501013B0", "0501120L0", "0501021G0"))
#> [1] "Penicillins"                                       
#> [2] "Quinolones"                                        
#> [3] "Cephalosporins, carbapenems and other beta-lactams"
